title: Apple launches HomeView hub as upgraded Siri AI takes centre stage
title_zh: 苹果推出HomeView智能中枢，升级版Siri AI成主角

image.credit: Photo by Laurenz Heymann on Unsplash
image.author: Laurenz Heymann

lead: Apple has unveiled a new smart home lineup led by the HomeView, an iPad-like hub that showcases an upgraded, more conversational Siri AI. The move pits the company against Amazon and OpenAI in an increasingly crowded market.
lead_zh: 苹果发布全新智能家居产品线，主打产品HomeView是一款类似iPad的中枢设备，搭载升级版、更善于对话的Siri AI。此举将使苹果在日益拥挤的市场中与亚马逊和OpenAI正面交锋。

paragraphs: Apple on Tuesday began showcasing a fresh round of smart home products, most notably the HomeView — an iPad-like device designed either to hang on walls or perch on tabletops and serve as a hub for other smart home gadgets. Priced from $299, it features a 7in screen and face recognition, and will help users control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. Preorders began today, with shipping expected from 13 November.

The launch was accompanied by updates to Apple's HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices, alongside a range of accessories from LG and Schneider Electric — including doorbells, cameras and thermostats — designed with Apple's help and managed through the Apple home app. Among them are a Schneider smart thermostat and LG home security devices, such as indoor and outdoor cameras, a doorbell camera, a floodlight camera and a smart lock unlockable via the app.

Apple is launching these products as it seeks to fend off competition from traditional rivals like Amazon — which has invested heavily in Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and last week launched premium tablets — as well as newer AI upstarts such as OpenAI, which harbours hardware ambitions of its own. Analysts have long identified two major hurdles for Apple: ensuring its devices work with a variety of third-party gadgets, and the limited ability of Siri to give useful answers.

Central to the HomeView is a revamped version of Siri AI, which Apple describes as more capable and conversational, drawing on personal context from apps like Messages and Calendar to provide more relevant answers. "It's powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core," the company said, "drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone's information private and secure."
Notably, the HomeView will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there owing to EU regulations, Apple said.
paragraphs_zh: 苹果周二开始展示新一轮智能家居产品，其中最引人注目的是HomeView——一款类似iPad的设备，既可挂在墙上，也可放在桌面上，充当其他智能家居设备的中枢。该设备起售价299美元，配备7英寸屏幕和面部识别功能，将帮助用户控制门铃、温控器和智能锁。苹果在这一市场已摸索十年，却始终未有重大突破。预购今日启动，预计11月13日起发货。
此次发布还伴随苹果HomePod智能音箱和Apple TV设备的更新，以及来自LG和施耐德电气的一系列配件——包括门铃、摄像头和温控器——这些配件在苹果协助下设计，并通过Apple home app进行管理。其中包括施耐德智能温控器和LG家庭安防设备，如室内外摄像头、门铃摄像头、泛光灯摄像头，以及可通过app解锁的智能锁。
苹果推出这些产品之际，正试图抵御来自传统竞争对手如亚马逊的竞争——亚马逊在Echo音箱和Ring门铃上投入巨资，并于上周推出高端平板电脑——以及像OpenAI这样怀有硬件野心的新兴AI初创公司。分析人士早已指出苹果面临的两大障碍：确保其设备兼容各种第三方产品，以及Siri提供有用答案的能力有限。
HomeView的核心是经过改造的Siri AI。苹果称其能力更强、更善于对话，能利用Messages和Calendar等应用中的个人上下文信息，提供更相关的答案。该公司表示：“它由Apple Intelligence驱动，以Siri AI为核心，利用iPhone上的个人上下文信息，帮助你找到所需内容、完成更多任务，同时确保每个人的信息私密安全。”
值得注意的是，苹果表示，HomeView将不会在欧盟销售，因为由于欧盟法规，Siri AI在该地区仍不可用。苹果于2016年首次发布用于控制智能设备的Home应用，2018年推出HomePod智能音箱，但这些产品与Alphabet的Google Home音箱和亚马逊的Echo系列存在竞争。

Apple unveils new smart home devices that showcase upgraded Siri AI
New products from Apple include the HomeView, an iPad-like device that acts as a hub for other smart home gadgets
Apple on Tuesday began showing off a ⁠new round of smart home products, including an iPad-like device dubbed the HomeView, meant to hang on walls or perch on tabletops ⁠and act as a hub for other smart home devices.
The HomeView device starts at $299 and will begin shipping next month. It will feature a 7in screen and face recognition, will help users ⁠control doorbells, thermostats and smart locks in a market where Apple has tinkered for a decade without major success. The device will also showcase Apple’s AI-upgraded Siri virtual ​assistant.
Preorders begin today and the devices are expected to be available starting 13 November.
Apple is launching these products as it ⁠tries to fend off competition from rivals, including traditional competitors like Amazon – which has invested heavily in ​its Echo speakers and Ring doorbells and ‌last week launched premium tablets – as well as newer AI upstarts like OpenAI that have hardware ambitions of their own.
Apple’s HomeView launch was accompanied by updates to its HomePod smart speaker and Apple TV devices. It also introduced a range of ‌accessories, including doorbells, cameras and thermostats, made by LG and Schneider Electric and designed with help from Apple.
The new line of devices are accessible and managed in the Apple home app. The accessories include a Schneider smart thermostat and LG home security devices including indoor and various outdoor cameras including a doorbell camera and floodlight camera as well as a smart lock. The lock can be unlocked using the Apple home app.
The HomeView device will not be sold in the European Union, because Siri AI remains unavailable there due to EU regulations, Apple said.
Apple first released its Home app to control smart gadgets in 2016, ⁠with HomePod smart speakers following in 2018, but those offerings are competing with ​Alphabet’s Google Home speakers and ​Amazon’s Echo line. Analysts said ​two major hurdles for Apple were making its devices work with a ​variety of third-party gadgets and ‌the limited ability ​of Siri to ​give useful answers.
The HomeView device includes a revamped version of Siri AI, the company announced. An Apple press release described the new version of Siri as more capable and conversational, using information from personal apps like Messages and Calendar to provide more relevant answers.
“It’s powered by Apple Intelligence with Siri AI at its core, drawing on personal context from your iPhone to help you find what you need and get more done, all while keeping everyone’s information private and secure,” the release said.
